declared.title: Becoming happier takes both a will and a proper way: An experimental longitudinal intervention to boost well-being.
declared.foundIn: OpenAlex search « trying to be happier really can work experimental » (2026-11-22); reports/chasing-happiness/counter-evidence.md (card 2)

population: undergraduates of a US public university, ethnically diverse (N = 355; full text), 8 months

findings.text: Students who joined knowing the study was about becoming happier, and those who kept up their effort, gained more from the happiness activities, not less

support.sentence: Our results indicate that initial self-selection makes a difference, but only in the two positive activity conditions, not the control, and that continued effort also makes a difference, but, again, only in the treatment conditions.

findings.text: Happiness activities work best when people know about them, endorse them and commit to them

support.sentence: We conclude that happiness interventions are more than just placebos, but that they are most successful when participants know about, endorse, and commit to the intervention.

limits: the will is not randomized: people chose a study announced as about happiness
small effects (« our rs spanned the low to mid .10s », full text)
allegiance: Lyubomirsky and Sheldon develop and promote the happiness activities they test
